page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-16 is a compute-focused instance within the cost-efficient E2 virtual machine family. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor operating at a base frequency of 2.2 GHz, it provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor features 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and a shared 16 MB L3 cache, supporting standard vector and cryptographic extensions including AVX, AES, and BMI2, while lacking AVX-512 and matrix extensions.

The configuration provides 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio suitable for compute-heavy applications that do not demand extensive in-memory footprints. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage and lacks integrated GPUs, relying exclusively on network-attached block storage for persistent disk access. Network interfaces provide standard virtual connectivity without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluation shows balanced mid-tier multi-threaded execution alongside constrained single-thread throughput. While stress-ng single-core performance registers in the top 25% among evaluated systems, overall Geekbench single-core results and single-threaded data compression tasks (such as gzip and bzip3) exhibit lower performance. In contrast, multi-threaded workloads, including software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and static web serving, operate firmly within middle-tier industry averages. Memory subsystem throughput reaches 71.67 GB/s read and 35.27 GB/s write on large uncached blocks.

The server offers resource efficiency by minimizing memory overhead relative to its 16 vCPU capacity. It is structurally aligned with batch processing, continuous integration build jobs, media transcoding, static web hosting, and microservices where execution throughput depends on parallel vCPU availability rather than high per-thread memory capacity or specialized hardware accelerators.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-16 is a compute-skewed virtual machine instance configured with 16 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1.0 GB per core ratio. Driven by an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz across 8 physical cores and 16 threads, the instance features AVX, AES, and BMI2 support, though it omits AVX-512 and hardware matrix extensions. System benchmarks place multi-core operations, Clang software builds, and static web serving within average baseline percentiles, while single-threaded compression and text processing show modest execution speeds. With no bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, the instance relies on network-attached storage. This hardware profile functions effectively for CPU-bound microservices, multi-threaded CI/CD pipelines, container orchestration nodes, and distributed batch processing workloads.
